html:
On the 1783 map, Mahratta states are the Maratha powers of north and central India, from Malwa up to Delhi. They were members of the Maratha Confederacy, led in name by the Peshwa at Pune, but they acted more and more on their own.

From the 1730s Maratha generals took Malwa and pushed north. Their families became the ruling houses of new states: the Scindias at Gwalior, the Holkars at Indore, the Gaekwads at Baroda. The defeat at the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 stopped them only for a while.

In 1783 they were at a high point. Mahadaji Shinde had made peace with Britain in the Treaty of Salbai of 1782, ending the First Anglo-Maratha War. Soon after he took charge of Delhi and the Mughal emperor. In Indore, Ahilyabai Holkar ruled wisely and rebuilt temples across India. The Rajput states paid them tribute. Britain broke Maratha power in the wars of 1803 and 1817 to 1818.
